discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moiré quantum materials)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: correlated electrons in two-dimensional moiré materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees collapses the electronic bandwidth, producing nearly flat bands in which interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. This work created an entirely new, tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological matter: a single device can be gate-tuned across insulating, superconducting, magnetic and Chern phases. It launched the field of twistronics and moiré quantum materials, which has since yielded orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and fractional Chern insulators at zero field in moiré systems. The combination of a clear theoretical prediction and decisive experiment transformed how physicists engineer and understand interacting electrons, and the platform has been taken up worldwide with lasting conceptual impact.
